chunks: Know that no man is more eager than I for the unity of the Ummah of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) and their solidarity.
I seek through it good reward and an honourable place to return to.
I shall fulfill what I have pledged upon myself, even though you may change from the sound state in which you left me.
For wretched is he who is denied the benefit of what he was given of intellect and experience.
ai.seo_question: What is Imam Ali's view on unity and the consequence of losing intellect?
ai.summary: In this response to Abu Musa al-Ashari regarding the arbitration at Siffin, Imam Ali (AS) highlights his personal priority for communal unity (Ulfah) over political victory, framing his patience as a means to secure divine reward. He underscores the practical wisdom of his stance by noting that the truly wretched are those who fail to utilize the intellect and experience granted to them, a key Shia emphasis on rational agency in leadership. This reflects the broader scholarly view of Ali’s arbitration as a strategic, albeit contested, effort to preserve the Ummah's cohesion.
